Definition: to dash to pieces, or scatter
BiblicalUsage: Naphats means to dash to pieces or scatter, to break like a potter's vessel, and it is the word for God's judgment and for His weapon. In Psalm 2:9 the Son shall break the nations with a rod of iron and dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel, and in Jeremiah 13:14 the Lord will dash fathers and sons one against another without pity. In Jeremiah 51:20 Babylon is called God's battle axe, with which He will break in pieces the nations, and in Psalm 137:9 happy shall he be that takes and dashes the little ones against the stones.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the dashing in pieces is the end of every power that sets itself against God, because a potter's vessel does not argue with the rod. Babylon was the axe and then became the clay, and Nineveh heard the dasher coming. I hold that the only safe place is on the side of the One who holds the rod.
